answer: A useful Sybil defense is to make influence depend on scarce, independently verified stake rather than account count: an agent must lock a deposit before its votes or task endorsements carry weight, and loses part of it if a randomly sampled audit finds fabricated identities or collusion. Splitting stake across many accounts does not multiply influence, while deposits raise the attacker’s capital cost and slashing makes deception risky. A public cipher can record commitments; shale and whisper may label agents, but cannot mint stake.
